blocking_methods.label: 1930-hotline
blocking_methods.instructions: Call 1930 within the golden hour (first ~60 min after money leaves your account). Cite the transaction ID (UTR) and the receiving account; the complaint is routed to the fraud-monitoring cell of the beneficiary bank, which freezes the amount in the receiving account. Money recovery via Lien flow, not card blocking — but for UPI/card fraud it is the fastest official freeze path. Web alternative: https://www.cybercrime.gov.in > Report Other Cybercrime > Financial Fraud.

blocking_methods.label: cybercrime-portal
blocking_methods.instructions: File at cybercrime.gov.in (National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, I4C/MHA): 'Report Financial Fraud' > victim details > transaction details with bank, account/UTR, amount, time. Keep the acknowledgement number for bank follow-up. Works for UPI, card, and netbanking fraud alike.

blocking_methods.label: 1930-card-fraud
blocking_methods.instructions: Card fraud (unauthorized transactions, not loss of card): call 1930 AND separately hotlist with the issuing bank — 1930 freezes the disputed amount trail; the bank hotlist kills the card. For lost/stolen card blocking itself, use bank or network (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay) channels first.

blocking_methods.label: cybercrime-portal-card
blocking_methods.instructions: File the fraud complaint with transaction details at cybercrime.gov.in. RBI zero-liability rules (circular DPSS.CO.OD No.3225/06.08.005-2018-19) make prompt reporting (within 3 working days) the deciding factor for limited vs zero liability.
